body.heading: The story behind the behaviour
paragraphs: The cashier who seems cold may be on hour nine of a shift. The friend who cancelled again may be caring for a parent. We usually judge behaviour with only half the story, and the missing half is almost always the human part.
Empathy starts with a simple question: what might today look like from inside their life? You will not always guess right, but the guessing itself slows down judgment.

body.heading: A small practice
paragraphs: Pick one person you found difficult this week and spend two minutes writing down what their day might contain — pressures, worries, hopes. It is not about excusing bad behaviour; it is about understanding it.
Understanding and agreeing are different things. You can understand exactly why someone acted as they did and still set a boundary. Empathy makes the boundary kinder, not weaker.

description: Imagining someone else's day — really imagining it — is the fastest way to soften a judgment.
